parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile federal document/entry layer with a state 'women's bill of rights' order. Traveler-facing exposures: consular cable allowing visa refusal on sex-discrepancy grounds (with possible fraud ineligibility), federal and state endorsement of birth-sex facility access (universal exposure, no documented working remedy here), custody placed by birth sex with a documented sexual assault and judicial dismissal of claims, and an under-19 care ban binding a visiting minor and their guardian. No statewide gender-identity hate-crime or public-accommodation statute leaves service denial thin on recourse. Protections are real but partial: national hate-crime, employment and housing coverage, marriage/adoption recognition, no sodomy law, courts that have enjoined several federal orders. No execution or routine-imprisonment pathway is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order and 2025 Supreme Court ruling permit sex-at-birth passport policy; X-marker processing halted; consular cable directs refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, and officers may consider lifetime fraud ineligibility. At least eight foreign governments issued travel advisories over identity-document rules.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; the policy is still litigated; fraud finding requires all four elements, has limited waivers and is never automatic. A visitor travels on their home passport, which state surgery-based marker rules do not govern.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport → federal visa/entry adjudication → possible refusal or referral; state marker rules (surgery affidavit, court order) apply only to locally issued documents, so they do not reach the foreign-passport holder.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: State houses incarcerated people by assigned sex: a transgender woman was celled with a convicted male sex offender, sexually assaulted, and a 2022 district judge dismissed her failure-to-treat, surgery-denial and failure-to-protect claims, calling injuries de minimis. Federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies from 2026; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; formal appeal rights exist; the case was litigated with counsel.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest (including a facility-related stop) drops the visitor into birth-sex custody where the documented institutional practice and judicial deference operate; federal custody adds its own regime.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: The 30 Aug 2023 executive order backs single-sex bathrooms and changing rooms and directs agencies to biological definitions; a federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; nationally 21+ units restrict facility access and 4 units criminalise it in certain circumstances. Facility exclusion is universal exposure for an outed visitor.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No facility-use criminal statute or enforcement provision is recorded for this state specifically; the order's scope and legality were contested by opponents.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State endorsement plus federal facility funding rules combine; whether this state is among the four criminalising units, and whether any city ordinance applies, is not documented.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for under-19s is banned (passed 33-15 May 2023, upheld 6-1 July 2024): a visiting minor cannot obtain it, nor can a visitor obtain it for a minor in their care. Federal funding freezes, lifted LGBTQ youth lifeline services and proposed insurance rules narrow options further.
care_services.protection: Adult care is not documented as banned; emergency or non-transition care denial is not documented; litigation is pending on several federal measures.
care_services.interaction: A traveller with a minor converts a care need into a legal dead end, with no in-state alternative and travel disruption as the practical outcome.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The state order declares biological sex fixed and ends state recognition of transgender people; federal orders describe care as 'mutilation' and direct investigation of 'gender ideology'. A May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups 'radically pro-transgender', and a Dec 2025 reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward memo never uses the phrase as a reward criterion, and the strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target those who merely disagree; national hate-crime law covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing lowers the threshold for discretionary stops and service refusals while formal legal protections remain partly operative.

minors_guardians.exposure: The under-19 care ban binds a visiting minor and any guardian seeking care for them; athletics bans and school-focused executive orders shape the climate. A name change for a minor requires court publication (locally issued documents only).
minors_guardians.protection: Marriage and adoption recognition for same-sex couples is settled by national law; visitor minors do not enter the school system or local marker processes.
minors_guardians.interaction: Care need plus birth-sex facility or custody practice means a family's exposure concentrates at clinics and any institutional contact.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide gender-identity hate-crime provision (1997 law silent on GI) and no statewide anti-discrimination statute covering public accommodations; only 23 units cover GI in bias statutes. No state-level trans violence statistics are recorded.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute since 2009 permits federal charges; national employment and fair-housing enforcement covers gender identity; the state hate-crime law was upheld in 2016 and applied to perceived-association bias.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Service refusal or harassment leaves only city ordinances (one city) or federal routes; violence can be federally charged but state-level pattern data is absent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Key national measures remain in litigation, so operative rules shift by travel date; the order's scope is contested; whether the state criminalises facility use, and whether agencies narrowed marker practice beyond the surgery statutes, is unrecorded. Absence of statewide GI discrimination coverage means no easy state remedy for service denial.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts have enjoined several federal orders; a legal aid FAQ tracks document rules; national employment/housing enforcement and one city ordinance give real, if partial, recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Partial recourse coexists with recurring institutional harm: courts worked against a detained trans woman here, which is exposure rather than mitigation.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra imposes a blanket, routinely enforced entry register with near-zero appeal. Here entry refusal is contingent on document discrepancy, the fraud finding is expressly never automatic, and challenges are live in court. No analogous universal exclusion register exists, so this sits well above 0.35.

Kestrel Isles shows discretionary secondary screening with administrative refusal and slow, rarely revised appeals — friction without institutionalised harm. This dossier adds facility exclusion by state policy, birth-sex custody with a documented sexual assault and judicial dismissal, and an under-19 care ban, so it sits below 0.55.

Meridia has trained border staff, a tribunal granting release and compensation, and尊重 for chosen markers. Here the state endorses birth-sex spaces, houses by birth sex with courts excusing harm, bans minor care, and lacks statewide GI discrimination coverage — materially lower than 0.75.

Drellia has mandatory registration and nightly hotel reporting creating durable discovery exposure without credible imprisonment. Similar in kind: universal facility exposure plus routine document scrutiny, but this jurisdiction adds documented custodial sexual assault with no remedy and criminal care denial for minors, placing it near or slightly above that level.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a layered system: federal document and entry rules raise discovery and refusal risk (documented foreign advisories), while the state's 2023 order endorses birth-sex facilities with no recorded enforcement provision here — universal exposure without a documented arrest pathway. Severity concentrates in custody (birth-sex placement, documented assault, claims dismissed — institutions as perpetrators with no working remedy) and in the under-19 care ban, which directly binds travelling families. Everyday exposure is moderated by real protections: national hate-crime, employment and housing coverage, marriage and adoption recognition, no sodomy law, and courts that have enjoined parts of the federal agenda. No imprisonment-for-being-trans or execution pathway is documented. Net: documented universal exposures plus thin state-level recourse, offset by functioning partial protections — Elevated Risk, upper half.
